samples.summary: Slides PUT block-style validation is advertised as covering "every text body" but skips `slide.notes`, `layouts[].placeholders`/`staticElements`, and `masters[]` — the same partial-coverage failure the task's own lessons doc calls out
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlide` only checks `Array.isArray(s.notes)` and then walks `s.elements`; `assertValidSlidesBody` checks `themes`/`masters`/`layouts` are arrays and never descends into them. But `Slide.notes: Block[]` (packages/slides/src/model/presentation.ts:45) and `Layout.placeholders: PlaceholderSpec[]` / `staticElements: Element[]` (presentation.ts:61-62) hold the same docs `Block`s reaching the same layout engine (see packages/slides/src/model/placeholder-blocks.ts). docs/design/rest-api.md (new text) states: "the same block-style value checks are applied to the docs `Block`s inside every text body — text elements, shape text, table cells and group children", and docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-lessons.md:71-73 records the rule "a validator that walks only one of the writer's inputs is worse than none, because it reads as coverage." A `NaN` marginTop or unknown alignment can still be PUT through `slides[i].notes[0].style` or through a layout placeholder.

samples.summary: Design doc names a helper that does not exist (`removeCellNodeStyle`); the shipped helper is `removeNodeStyle` and is not cell-specific
samples.evidence: docs-tables.md:184 says "Yorkie has no single-node removal, so `removeCellNodeStyle` (`yorkie-doc-store.ts`) converts the path to an index". The implementation is `function removeNodeStyle(...)` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:273) and it is also used for block-type attribute removal at line 1459, not just cells. Nested design docs are not covered by the backticked-path CI check, so nothing else will catch this drift.

samples.summary: Substantial scope beyond the originating issue (#728 color reset): backend PUT block-style/header/footer/inline/table-cell validation, a new shared CRDT attribute codec module, DOCX `w:jc` lookup hardening, PPTX `listLevel`/modifier coercion
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md's Plan and its single acceptance criterion ("reset the text color → the text is uncolored") cover the toolbar reset, the renderer `resolveStoredColor` guard, and the DOCX/PPTX *color* normalizers only. The new `assertValidBlockStyle`/`assertValidHeaderFooter`/`assertValidTextBodyBlocks` walkers, `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts`, `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS`, `ALGN` Map and `listLevelAttr` are not plan items; they are recorded only after the fact in the lessons doc. The Plan checklist was never updated to declare them, so the task doc understates what shipped.

samples.evidence: docs-header-footer.md:300-301 shows `{ type: 'header', marginFromEdge: '48' }` as the persisted node shape; `serializeMarginFromEdgeAttrs` now emits `{}` when the value is absent/non-finite and the reader defaults to `DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE`. Only docs-collaboration.md records the new partial-on-the-wire contract; the header/footer doc that owns this attribute was not updated.

samples.summary: Alias-only indirection layers: `toDocxHexColor` is a pure re-export of `toRgbHexColor`, and both Yorkie stores alias the shared codec (`const serializeBlockStyle = serializeBlockStyleAttrs`)
samples.evidence: `export function toDocxHexColor(color) { return toRgbHexColor(color); }` adds a second public name (and a second test suite) for identical behavior; likewise `const serializeBlockStyle = serializeBlockStyleAttrs; const parseBlockStyle = parseBlockStyleAttrs;` in both packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts. Importing the canonical names directly at the call sites would keep one name per concept.

verdict.reason:
I could not find any counterexample: no validation of the docs `Block`s inside `slide.notes`, `layouts[].placeholders` / `layouts[].staticElements`, or `masters[]` exists anywhere in the write path.

Facts I verified myself:
- `docs-content.controller.ts` is the ONLY file in the repo containing `assertValid*` slides validators (grep for `assertValid|isBlockAlignment|BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS` across the tree returns only this controller, `@wafflebase/docs` crdt-attrs, and review/task docs).
- `assertValidSlidesBody` (controller.ts:452-462) only checks `themes`/`masters`/`layouts`/`slides` are arrays and then descends into `slides` alone; it never walks `layouts` or `masters`.
- `assertValidSlide` (controller.ts:485-501) checks `Array.isArray(s.notes)` and then loops only over `s.elements`; `notes` blocks are never handed to `assertValidBlockStyle`/`assertValidTextBodyBlocks`.
- The payload really does carry docs `Block`s there: `Slide.notes: Block[]` (packages/slides/src/model/presentation.ts:45) and `Layout.placeholders: PlaceholderSpec[]` = `ElementInit & {...}` / `staticElements: Element[]` (presentation.ts:52-63, element.ts:624-628), i.e. TextElements with the same `data.blocks` shape the covered arms validate.
- Nothing downstream compensates: `writeSlidesRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:97-109) assigns `root.masters`, `root.layouts`, `root.slides` verbatim with no normalization, and the global `ValidationPipe` in packages/backend/src/main.ts:65-72 cannot act on `@Body() body: unknown` (no DTO metatype).
- The advertised guarantee is in the design doc: docs/design/rest-api.md:244-250 says on a slides body "the same block-style value checks are applied to the docs `Block`s inside every text body", and docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-lessons.md:67-73 records the repo's own rule that a validator walking only some of the writer's inputs "is worse than none, because it reads as coverage."

Nuance (does not change the verdict): the doc sentence enumerates "text elements, shape text, table cells and group children", which one could read as scoping the promise to slide elements — but layout placeholder text bodies are still text bodies reaching the same layout engine, and the lessons-doc rule is stated in terms of the writer's inputs, so the partial-coverage fit violation stands as a `major` under the design-fit rubric.
